biography: Carlos Novak, a name whispered with anticipation in Argentinian racing circles, hails from the bustling streets of Buenos Aires. Unlike most racers who grew up karting, Novak’s introduction to speed came through the underground world of 'picadas' – illegal street races that throbbed with adrenaline and danger. He learned car control the hard way, dodging stray dogs and weaving through traffic under the cloak of night. His raw talent couldn't be ignored for long. A chance encounter with a retired racing engineer, impressed by Novak's audacious driving during one such race, led to an opportunity to compete in a local Formula Renault series. Despite lacking the polished background of his rivals, Novak’s innate ability and fearless attitude quickly made him a fan favorite. Now, at 20, he's taking on the challenge of single-seater racing without team support, relying on the backing of small sponsors and his own sheer grit, a true testament to his self-made journey. He is considered a rising star, but also a gamble, a sentiment he embraces with open arms.
drivingStyle: Novak’s driving style is as flamboyant as his personality. He's an aggressive late-braker, often pushing the limits of grip to the point of near-disaster. Tire management isn’t exactly his forte; he prefers an all-out attack from the start, relying on raw speed to compensate. Under pressure, Novak tends to either thrive, pulling off stunning overtakes, or crack spectacularly, making costly errors. He's a high-risk, high-reward driver, a showman who prioritizes excitement over consistency.

rivalries.reason: A veteran of the sport, Rossi publicly criticized Novak's aggressive tactics, leading to on-track clashes and heated exchanges in the media.
Vargas, a fellow Argentinian, sees Novak as a threat to his established position in the racing hierarchy, resulting in intense competition and personal animosity.
Dubois and Novak were involved in a controversial collision that cost Dubois a race victory. The incident remains unresolved, fueling a bitter rivalry.

quirks: Always wears a lucky 'alfajor' charm inside his racing suit.
Refuses to start a race without listening to a specific tango song.
Has a habit of sketching car designs on napkins before important races, believing it helps him visualize the track.
famousQuote: Life's too short to drive slow. If you're not pushing the limit, what's the point?
careerHighlight: Winning the Argentinian Formula Renault Championship in his rookie season, a victory secured with a daring last-lap overtake that cemented his reputation as a fearless competitor.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in a crucial race due to a late-braking error, costing him valuable championship points and attracting criticism for his overly aggressive style.
